k:audio-multimodal-instructions@1.3:7a5a.excerpt:
## Language and repeated audio
Confirm the requested language and any permitted switching before recording a language mismatch. A familiar accent or an ordinary loanword is not automatically a defect.

When a phrase repeats, record where it occurs. If feasible, compare the downloaded file with player output. Do not call it a confirmed generation defect until the available evidence distinguishes generation from playback.

k:audio-multimodal-instructions@1.3:1c6d.excerpt:
## Playback and unavailable content
- If the player fails to load or start, report a tool incident with the task ID.
- A visible waveform with no playback is still a playback/tool incident; the waveform alone does not establish that the recording is silent.
- Do not score unavailable audio as a model-quality failure or make a content-based Quarantine (QN) decision solely because playback is unavailable.
- Capture the browser/error state and whether another clip plays. An old workaround must be checked against the current symptoms; recurrence alone does not establish which fix was tried or why it failed.
- Handling guidance does not confirm that playback has been repaired or that an affected task can be evaluated.

k:audio-multimodal-faq@1.1:f72aa6db.excerpt:
## Language and TTS

### Q: The generated speech is in the wrong language. Is that a playback failure?
Confirm the requested language and permitted switching. If the recording itself contains an unrequested language mismatch, record it as a language-quality issue rather than a playback failure.

k:audio-multimodal-instructions@1.3:2792.excerpt:
## Project purpose
Evaluate audio intelligibility, correspondence with the reference transcript, and requested language. Distinguish recording/model defects from Label Tool (LT) failures.

The team lead requested language checks in all four threads; follow-up confirmations are still missing, while the current FAQ already explains how to handle a confirmed unrequested language mismatch.

severity.rationale: Five distinct reporters describe comparable unexpected-language behavior in the same batch and day, suggesting a broader labeling-quality risk; the reports do not establish a shared cause.

recommended_action.draft_text:
For the language reports: two tutors report Spanish despite requested English, including AUDIO-5641; a QA tutor reports Spanish after an English prompt. A tutor and a QA tutor report halfway switches; the tutor also reports speech differing from English reference text.

Please confirm the requested language, any permitted switching, and what the speaker actually says, as I requested in each thread. Under the current FAQ, if the recording itself contains an unrequested language mismatch, record it as a language-quality issue rather than a playback failure. An English prompt or reference alone does not complete those checks.
recommended_action.scope_note: This reminder supplies current handling, not a finding about any individual task or a confirmed technical cause.
recommended_action.label: Post a reminder
recommended_action.instruction: Post a short reminder explaining the current FAQ's conditional handling of language mismatches, without declaring the reported recordings defective.
recommended_action.rationale: The current FAQ answers the handling question without requiring a new rule. Its confirmation requirement preserves the distinction between an unrequested mismatch and permitted bilingual speech.

card.reasoning: What the evidence shows: A QA tutor reports that an English prompt produced Spanish audio and asks for the correct handling. Two tutors report Spanish speech despite requested English narration; one identifies AUDIO-5641. A tutor reports TTS switching languages halfway through and, in a separate thread, rendered speech using another language despite English reference text. A QA tutor reports a speaker switching languages halfway despite an English-only prompt. The team lead asks in each of the four threads for confirmation of the requested language and what the speaker actually says, to rule out an intentional bilingual prompt. A QA tutor asks whether the file plays correctly aside from the language issue in the first clarification thread; a different QA tutor asks the same question in the AUDIO-5641 thread. A QA tutor asks whether a language switch was requested in the tutor-started language-switch thread; a different QA tutor asks whether switching or bilingual reading was permitted in the QA-started language-switch thread. The current FAQ requires confirming the requested language and permitted switching; if the recording itself contains an unrequested language mismatch, record it as a language-quality issue rather than a playback failure. The provided threads end with the team lead's requests and contain no subsequent confirmations or handling resolution. Thread status, read from each thread's own messages: unresolved ×4. Agent 1's earlier labels (an input, not evidence): unresolved ×4; 1 of 4 were not verified by Agent 1.
